pencereler.0-5: Minutes after take-off, a jumbo jet exploded off Long Island. It broke apart and
pencereler.5-12: fell into the ocean, killing everyone aboard. Investigators traced the blast to the centre fuel tank. That tank was
pencereler.12-20: nearly empty. Heat from the air-conditioning units warmed the vapour inside. Warm fuel vapour is far easier to ignite than liquid fuel.
pencereler.20-30: A spark, most likely from wiring, set it off. New rules now require airliners to make those tanks far less flammable.

segmentler.metin: TWA Flight 800 exploded shortly after take-off from New York.
It took only fuel vapour in a nearly empty centre tank.
So how could fuel vapour in a nearly empty centre tank do this?

The answer is ignition of flammable fuel-air vapour in the centre wing tank, most likely from a wiring fault — and it is why the FAA required systems that reduce fuel tank flammability, such as nitrogen inerting.
